title: Euclidean weak Sobolev graphs and smoothing with controlled support
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $m\geq1$, $r\geq0$ and $s\geq0$ be integers. Let $L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$ mean Lebesgue-measurable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality with finite integral of the squared Euclidean norm. Let $\mathcal D'(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$ mean componentwise continuous linear functionals on compactly supported smooth scalar test functions, with their usual test-function topology. Integration against test functions defines an injective linear map $L^2(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)\to\mathcal D'(\mathbf R^m,\mathbf R^r)$; $L^2$ convergence implies convergence against every test function. Define $W^{s,2}$ to consist of $f\in L^2$ for which each distributional derivative $\partial^\alpha f$, $|\alpha|\leq s$, is represented by an $L^2$ function, where $\langle\partial^\alpha f,\varphi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int f\,\partial^\alpha\varphi$. The inner product $\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\int\langle\partial^\alpha f,\partial^\alpha g\rangle$ makes $W^{s,2}$ a Hilbert space, including $W^{0,2}=L^2$. Its derivative graph is closed: if $f_n\in W^{s,2}$ and $\partial^\alpha f_n\to g_\alpha$ in $L^2$ for every $|\alpha|\leq s$, then $g_0\in W^{s,2}$ and $\partial^\alpha g_0=g_\alpha$. If $K\subset\Omega\subset\mathbf R^m$, with $K$ compact and $\Omega$ open, and $f\in W^{s,2}$ vanishes almost everywhere off $K$, there exist a compact $K'$ with $K\subseteq K'\subset\Omega$ and $f_n\in C_c^\infty(\Omega,\mathbf R^r)$ all supported in $K'$ such that $\|f_n-f\|_{W^{s,2}}\to0$.

proof.text: For a compactly supported smooth scalar test $\varphi$, continuity and compact support make $\varphi$ square integrable: apply [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable] to $|\varphi|^2$, viewed as complex valued. By [lem-sfb-real-l2-hilbert-pairing], each component obeys $|\int f_j\varphi|\leq\|f_j\|_2\|\varphi\|_2$. This defines a representative-independent linear functional. On tests supported in a fixed compact $C$ the bound $\|\varphi\|_2\leq\operatorname{vol}(C)^{1/2}\sup_C|\varphi|$ proves continuity for the usual test-function topology (the locally convex inductive-limit topology of the fixed-compact-support spaces). The same estimate gives convergence against each test under $L^2$ convergence. Also $\int_C|f_j|\leq\|f_j\|_2\operatorname{vol}(C)^{1/2}$, by scalar Cauchy–Schwarz with $1_C$, so $f_j$ is locally integrable. If all tests pair to zero, apply [lem-sfb-smooth-test-ae-separation] on $U=\mathbf R^m$ to the complex-valued function $f_j+0i$. It vanishes almost everywhere. There are finitely many components, so $f=0$ almost everywhere. Thus the distribution map is injective, including the zero-rank case.

proof.text: Suppose $\partial^\alpha f_n\to g_\alpha$ in $L^2$, including $f_n\to g_0$. For each test $\varphi$, scalar Cauchy–Schwarz from [lem-sfb-real-l2-hilbert-pairing] passes to the limit in the defining identity and gives $\int (g_\alpha)_j\varphi=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int (g_0)_j\partial^\alpha\varphi$. Here $\partial^\alpha\varphi$ is again a compactly supported smooth test. Therefore $g_\alpha$ represents $\partial^\alpha g_0$, so $g_0\in W^{s,2}$. Uniqueness follows from step 1. This proves the asserted closed graph.

proof.text: Distributional differentiation and the injection are linear, hence $W^{s,2}$ is a vector space and its derivative graph is a linear subspace of the finite product indexed by $\{\alpha\in\mathbf N^m:|\alpha|\leq s\}$. Pull back the sum of the $L^2$ inner products of [lem-sfb-real-l2-hilbert-pairing]. It is positive definite because the summand $\alpha=0$ has squared norm $\|f\|_2^2$. If $(f_n)$ is Cauchy for the sum norm, every derivative sequence is Cauchy in $L^2$, so it has a limit $g_\alpha$ by that node's completeness. Step 2 identifies these as derivatives of $g_0$; the finite sum of their squared errors tends to zero. This proves completeness and the Hilbert assertion. At $s=0$ the sole derivative is the identity, giving $W^{0,2}=L^2$ with its original norm.

proof.text: If $K$ is empty, then $f=0$ in $L^2$; take $K'=\varnothing$ and all approximants zero. Otherwise, for each $a\in K$ choose $r_a>0$ with $\overline B(a,3r_a)\subset\Omega$, and take a finite cover of $K$ by $B(a_i,r_i)$. Set $\delta=\min_i r_i>0$ and $K'=\bigcup_i\overline B(a_i,2r_i)$. These are finitely many compact Euclidean balls inside $\Omega$. If $y\in K$ and $|z|\leq\delta$, choose $i$ with $|y-a_i|<r_i$; then $|y+z-a_i|<2r_i$, so $K+\overline B(0,\delta)\subset K'$. By [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-ball-bump] with center $0$ and radii $1/2,1$, choose $0\leq\beta\leq1$, smooth, equal to one on $\overline B(0,1/2)$ and supported in $\overline B(0,1)$. Its integral $c$ is finite by [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable] (embed the real function in $\mathbf C$) and positive since $\beta=1$ on a ball of positive measure. Set $\rho=\beta/c$ and $\rho_\epsilon(z)=\epsilon^{-m}\rho(z/\epsilon)$. Thus $\rho$ is a nonnegative integrable unit-mass kernel for the later approximate-identity application; each $\rho_\epsilon$ is smooth with support in $\overline B(0,\epsilon)$.

proof.text: For $\epsilon>0$ put $f_\epsilon(x)=\int\rho_\epsilon(x-y)f(y)\,dy$. Step 1 gives local integrability of $f$, so [lem-sfb-euclidean-smooth-kernel-convolution] makes this an everywhere-defined smooth function. Its first derivative differentiates the kernel. Iterating that same formula with the compact smooth scalar kernels $\partial^\gamma\rho_\epsilon$ gives, by induction on $|\alpha|$, $\partial^\alpha f_\epsilon(x)=\int(\partial^\alpha\rho_\epsilon)(x-y)f(y)\,dy$: the base is the defining integral, and one more coordinate derivative differentiates $\partial^\gamma\rho_\epsilon$. Every derivative kernel is smooth with support in the original compact support, so the cited lemma applies at each induction step.

proof.text: Write $g_\alpha$ for the $L^2$ representative of $\partial^\alpha f$. In its defining weak identity use the test $y\mapsto\rho_\epsilon(x-y)$. Its $y$ derivative is $(-1)^{|\alpha|}(\partial^\alpha\rho_\epsilon)(x-y)$, so the two signs cancel and step 5 yields $\partial^\alpha f_\epsilon(x)=\int\rho_\epsilon(x-y)g_\alpha(y)\,dy$. The change $z=x-y$ identifies this integral with $A_\epsilon g_\alpha$ of [lem-sfb-l2-compact-kernel-approximation]. In particular it is in $L^2$. These classical derivatives also are distributional derivatives: componentwise apply [lem-sfb-scalar-integrable-integration-by-parts], embedding real scalars in $\mathbf C$, once for each coordinate derivative and moving it onto the test. All products in that lemma are smooth with compact support from the test or its derivative, hence integrable by [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable]. Repeating produces exactly $(-1)^{|\alpha|}$. Consequently $f_\epsilon\in W^{s,2}$, with all its weak derivatives represented by the displayed convolutions.

proof.text: For $0<\epsilon\leq\delta$ and $x\notin K'$, one has $\rho_\epsilon(x-y)=0$ for every $y\in K$, by the buffer inclusion of step 4. For almost every $y\notin K$ one has $f(y)=0$. Thus the integrand defining $f_\epsilon(x)$ vanishes almost everywhere and $f_\epsilon(x)=0$. Since $K'$ is closed, the topological support of $f_\epsilon$ is contained in $K'$. Restriction to $\Omega$ is therefore in $C_c^\infty(\Omega,\mathbf R^r)$, with extension by zero equal to this same globally smooth function.

proof.text: Take $\epsilon_n=\delta/(n+1)$ for $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-l2-compact-kernel-approximation] to the single kernel $\rho$ of step 4 and separately to each $g_\alpha$, $|\alpha|\leq s$. By step 6, $\|\partial^\alpha f_{\epsilon_n}-g_\alpha\|_2\to0$. There are only finitely many such multi-indices, hence $\|f_{\epsilon_n}-f\|_{W^{s,2}}^2=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\|\partial^\alpha f_{\epsilon_n}-g_\alpha\|_2^2\to0$. Step 7 supplies the common compact support $K'\subset\Omega$. The argument also applies at $s=0$; at $r=0$ every vector and every approximant is zero.
